chief_complaint: widespread muscle pain, chronic fatigue, and poor sleep
hpi_details: A 41-year-old male presents with widespread muscle pain, chronic fatigue, and poor sleep persisting at a similar level for the past 6 months.
ideas: He thinks his widespread body aches and exhaustion stem from severe workplace burnout and months of poor sleep.
concerns: He is worried that he might have a serious hidden neurological disease like multiple sclerosis that will eventually make him unable to provide for his family.
expectations: He hopes to have comprehensive blood tests to check his vitamin levels and receive a prescription sleep aid to help him rest.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Fibromyalgia is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes diagnosis per ACR 2016 criteria after excluding secondary causes, followed by exercise/CBT with pharmacotherapy for inadequate response, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: widespread muscle pain, chronic fatigue, and poor sleep
Key HPI features: A 41-year-old male presents with widespread muscle pain, chronic fatigue, and poor sleep persisting at a similar level for the past 6 months.
Objective/Exam findings: Vitals normal. No joint swelling, warmth, or synovitis on exam. Normal strength and neurologic exam. No lymphadenopathy or rash.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Fibromyalgia.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Hypothyroidism without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Objective joint swelling.
management_principles: Diagnose using ACR 2016 criteria (Widespread Pain Index, Symptom Severity Scale, symptoms present at a similar level for at least 3 months) rather than tender-point counting alone
Exclude secondary causes with basic labs (TSH, CBC, ESR/CRP, CK) since fibromyalgia is a clinical diagnosis of exclusion
First-line treatment is patient education, graded aerobic exercise, CBT, and sleep hygiene
Consider pharmacotherapy (duloxetine, pregabalin, or low-dose amitriptyline) for inadequate response, individualized by comorbidities.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: A 41-year-old male presents with widespread muscle pain, chronic fatigue, and poor sleep persisting at a similar level for the past 6 months.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. No joint swelling, warmth, or synovitis on exam. Normal strength and neurologic exam. No lymphadenopathy or rash.
reference_soap.assessment: Widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and non-restorative sleep for 6 months without objective joint swelling or inflammatory findings, meeting ACR 2016 criteria features for fibromyalgia; hypothyroidism and inflammatory conditions should be excluded with basic labs.
reference_soap.plan: Confirm using the ACR 2016 fibromyalgia criteria and obtain basic labs (TSH, CBC, ESR/CRP, CK) to exclude secondary causes. Initiate first-line management: patient education, graded aerobic exercise, CBT, and sleep hygiene. Consider pharmacotherapy (duloxetine, pregabalin, or low-dose amitriptyline) for inadequate response to non-pharmacologic measures.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Fibromyalgia
Select appropriate diagnostic workup (ACR 2016 criteria, exclusion labs) for Fibromyalgia
Implement evidence-based management plan: Aerobic exercise, CBT, Duloxetine or low-dose Amitriptyline

teaching.one_liner: Central sensitization of pain pathways causing widespread muscle pain, chronic fatigue, and poor sleep without inflammation.

must_ask.say: Is the pain widespread, all over your body?
Do you wake up feeling rested?
How long has this been going on?

history.answer: I've been dealing with aching pain all over my body, along with constant exhaustion and terrible sleep for the past six months.
The aching is everywhere, in my neck, shoulders, back, hips, and knees on both sides equally.
It started gradually about six months ago, and it has stayed at about the same level ever since.
It is a constant, dull, deep ache that usually sits around a five or six out of ten.
No, I haven't noticed any joint swelling, redness, or warmth anywhere.
I feel stiff when I first get out of bed, but it usually loosens up after fifteen or twenty minutes of moving around.
Physical overexertion and stressful days make the pain flare up, whereas warm showers and light stretching take the edge off.
I can walk and bear weight normally, but everyday tasks feel exhausting and leave me drained.
No, I haven't had any fevers, chills, or night sweats.
No, there was no trauma, fall, or twisting injury, and my joints don't pop, lock, or catch.
No, I've never experienced sudden severe joint attacks like gout in the past.
I feel worn out and exhausted all the time no matter how much I rest, but my weight has been stable.
My sleep is very poor; I wake up multiple times during the night and always wake up feeling unrefreshed.
I've had trouble concentrating at work lately and feel like I'm living with constant brain fog and forgetfulness.
No, I haven't had any skin rashes, mouth ulcers, hair loss, red eyes, or dry mouth and eyes.
No, my back doesn't wake me up at night, and I don't have heel pain or sausage-like swelling of my fingers or toes.
No, I haven't had any recent bouts of diarrhea, painful urination, penile discharge, or sore throat.
I eat a balanced diet without bingeing on meat or seafood, and I don't take water pills.
No, I've never taken steroids or immunosuppressants, and I've never had joint injections or joint surgery.
I am in a monogamous relationship with my partner and haven't had any new sexual partners.
I thought I was just suffering from total burnout and chronic fatigue because of crazy stress at my job.
I'm terrified that there's some serious nerve disease eating away at me and that I won't be able to support my family.
I'm hoping you'll run full blood tests to check my vitamin and hormone levels and prescribe something so I can finally sleep.
I've always been healthy overall with no chronic medical conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I'm not currently taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter pain relievers, or supplements.
No, I don't have any allergies to medications.
I don't smoke and have never smoked.
I only drink socially, having a beer or two on the weekend.
I work as an accountant at an office desk job, and I live with my wife.
There is no family history of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, gout, or chronic widespread pain.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.6°C, SpO2 99% on room air.
Alert, oriented, appears fatigued and mildly uncomfortable, but in no acute distress.
No cervical, supraclavicular, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable.
Normal size, symmetric, non-tender, with no palpable nodules or goiter.
No joint erythema, warmth, effusion, or synovitis; full active and passive range of motion across all peripheral joints, with diffuse tenderness over surrounding soft tissues.
Full cervical and thoracolumbar range of motion without focal bony tenderness, with mild diffuse tenderness over paraspinal muscles.
Skin is clear without rashes, psoriasis plaques, malar erythema, tophi, or nail pitting.
Normal muscle tone and 5/5 strength symmetrically across all major upper and lower extremity muscle groups.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation symmetrically across all dermatomes.
Biceps, triceps, patellar, and Achilles deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally with downgoing plantar reflexes.
Gait is steady, coordinated, and non-antalgic without assistive devices.
